money-and-cost.rate_and_date: A$1 = 0.6293 EUR (Reserve Bank of Australia, 30 October 2026)
money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: Cash declaration: French Customs requires anyone carrying cash, bearer negotiable instruments, prepaid cards or gold worth 10,000 euros or more (or the equivalent) to declare it, whether or not they live in France. 10,000 euros is about A$15,891 at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026 (A$1 = EUR 0.6293). Amounts of 50,000 euros or more also need proof of where the money came from. Declare online (the DALIA service, up to 30 days ahead) or on a paper form. Failing to declare can bring a fine of up to 50% of the amount and seizure of the cash. The page applies Article L152-1 to movements between mainland France and the overseas departments and EU Regulation 2018/1672 to movements across the EU border.

items.text: French Guiana is part of France and French drug law applies: using any narcotic, cannabis included, is a criminal offence.

Refusing tests to identify a drug: up to 2 years and EUR 30,000.
